slice: Isolate native Float64 IN execution from SQL planning

decision.finding: The standalone native-expression executable reproduces cross-process timing and branch-miss variation with matching occupied table slots. SQL parsing, planning and execution-plan scheduling are not necessary conditions for this observation.
decision.controls: Both within-process primary median controls pass. Seed 4 within-process mean excludes zero (+0.003262% to +0.022359%); seed 0 cross-process mean exceeds the existing +/-1% bound (-0.457099% to +1.424153%). All groups and both failed controls are retained.
decision.scope: This rebuild uses one retained table and pre-normalized input, changing executable layout and measured work. It does not establish a hardware or hashbrown defect, compare the type-inference candidate, or resolve the original positive release interval.

summary.input_validation: Independently reconstructed ordered 64-bit fingerprint and seven exact special-value bit patterns; finite input check, exact row-by-row Boolean output check.

method.question: Does the native Float64 IN expression still vary within and across processes after removing SQL planning, execution-plan scheduling and per-query table construction?
method.implementation: A standalone synchronous Rust example calls the existing InListExpr::try_new_from_array and PhysicalExpr::evaluate. It uses the same 1048576-row permutation, Float64 values, 128 constants and 8192-row batches as the SQL case. Arrow add_wrapping with scalar zero normalizes the input once before measurement. The native filter, original RandomState implementation, shared-seed diagnostic and cold complete-slot trace are byte-identical to the preceding build.
method.design: Exactly sixteen groups of four fresh processes. Each prior native seed input (0 and 4) receives eight groups fully crossing every preparation position with both ABBA/BAAB execution orders, verified by the existing prepared_phase_schedule.py helper. Both historical scenario labels refer to the same standalone executable; they distinguish only the two seed strata. Each process retains one table and the input batches, checks every output row before/after measurement, performs 32 warmups, then records 261 quartets (1044 executions). Timing labels are assigned afterward as alternating ABBA/BAAB by quartet and process slot, so the executable never branches on a label. Preserve every timing and counter.
method.validation: Check the expected 994522 matches against both frozen ANSI captures. Verify all rows, native SET dispatch, zero normalization, input bit fingerprint, one full table trace and 128 exact member bit patterns. Reject invalid CLI modes and sample settings. Eight short gated smoke processes must pass before freezing the fixed collection.
method.analysis: Report the full timing distributions and process-level median/mean controls within and across processes. Analyze each seed stratum separately. For both cross-process and within-process controls, bootstrap complete four-process groups within the four balanced schedule blocks, with 10000 resamples and seed 88. Within-process group statistics are medians of the four process estimates; both timing labels use exactly the same retained table. Keep the historical +/-1% and include-zero control criteria unchanged. Hardware counters aggregate the entire execution phase and cannot assign misses to individual within-process labels. Compare all cold table traces and addresses; mismatches remain findings, not exclusions.
method.stopping_rule: One fixed sixteen-group collection, no outcome-based extensions, input replacement or discarded runs. No other machine work during timing. Restore shared source, lock and executable slots in finally. No global settings change.
limits: This rebuild has different executable layout and omits input normalization from the measured loop. Its absolute speed is not a production improvement.
One retained table differs from the original sequence of independently constructed tables. Failure to reproduce variation cannot by itself blame SQL planning or scheduling.
This experiment neither compares the type-inference candidate nor changes its deferred adoption decision.
method.design_revision_before_measurement: The initial four-group sketch was expanded before any benchmark run because time-control interpretation requires the already established fully crossed schedule. Both initial design files are retained.

analysis.scope: Same-executable native-expression controls. Counter totals are per execution phase, not per within-process timing label. No candidate/original or production speedup estimate.

source_audit.execution_path: Synchronous main constructs InListExpr from a Float64 array and calls PhysicalExpr::evaluate on pre-normalized RecordBatches. The 128-member list bypasses the native short-list path and reaches Float64StaticFilter::contains. There is no SessionContext, SQL parser, logical planner, execution-plan scheduler or Tokio runtime in this program.
source_audit.build_scope: The existing experiment workspace and frozen override inputs are reused, compiling the new example temporarily in the decimal_bench target slot. Unused workspace dependencies may be built; the example does not call their SQL/Sail entrypoints. Shared sources and executable slots were restored and hash-checked.
source_audit.validation: Every output row is checked before and after measurement. Normalized input is checked with an independently reconstructed ordered 64-bit fingerprint and seven exact special-value bit patterns; the fingerprint is finite, not a collision-free comparison of every input row. The frozen SQL case supplies the expected 994522 matching rows in both ANSI settings.
source_audit.measurement_scope: One retained table and 128 input batches per process. Arrow add-zero normalization, table construction, validation and output serialization are outside the measured phase. Per-phase perf counters include the FIFO handshake and timing-loop overhead.
source_audit.wording_correction: Post-collection clarification only: the initial source audit and frozen verification stdout overstate the input check as every input bit. Their original contents are retained; the check implementation and measured data are unchanged.

reproduction.setup: Reuse the frozen table-slot diagnostic dependencies and lockfile, replacing only the benchmark source with examples/native_in_bench.rs. The recorded build temporarily uses the decimal_bench target slot; the build script restores shared files and executable slots in finally. Keep the fully crossed schedule, seeds and criteria fixed before collection. The standalone native_in_bench example also runs against the normal experiment dependencies, without reproducing these exact diagnostic identities.
reproduction.offline_check: Extract scripts["check-archive.py"] from the gzip JSON to a temporary file, then run python3 CHECK.py /path/to/float-type-native-in-results.json.
